subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Show that the lines whose direction cosines are given by l+m+n=0, 2mn+3nl−5lm=0 are perpendicular to each other.

mark_split.label: Eliminate l to get a quadratic in m/n
Read off the product of its roots
Eliminate n to get a quadratic in l/m

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say whether you need to find the two lines, and what quantity you test at the end.

steps.label: Eliminate l to get a quadratic in m/n
steps.margin_note: Two marks, and the move that makes this question different from its neighbours. The two lines are NEVER found — only the PRODUCTS of their direction ratios are needed, and those come from the quadratics' roots. Divide through by n² to get a quadratic in m/n.
steps.memory_tip: The two lines are NEVER found here — only the PRODUCTS of their ratios are needed.
lines: Given l + m + n = 0  ⇒  l = −(m + n)  ……(1);

recall.must_convey: That eliminating l gives 5m² + 4mn − 3n² = 0, divided through by n² to become a quadratic in m/n.
accept: eliminate l and divide by n squared to get a quadratic in m over n
substitute the linear relation and collect
five m over n squared plus four m over n minus three equals zero
l ni eliminate chesi n square tho divide cheyyali
this gives a quadratic in m by n

steps.why: The perpendicularity test needs only l₁l₂ + m₁m₂ + n₁n₂, and each product is the PRODUCT OF THE ROOTS of one of these quadratics — so the individual lines never have to be found. That is what keeps a seven-mark question short.
common_mistakes: Solving for the two lines explicitly, which is far more work than the question needs.
Dividing by m² instead of n² and getting the reciprocal roots.

steps.label: Read off the product of its roots
steps.margin_note: One mark. For ax² + bx + c = 0 the product of the roots is c/a. The two roots here are m₁/n₁ and m₂/n₂, so their product gives m₁m₂ against n₁n₂.
steps.memory_tip: For ax² + bx + c = 0 the product of roots is c/a, and the roots here are m₁/n₁ and m₂/n₂.
lines: This is a quadratic equation in m/n; its roots are taken as  m₁/n₁,  m₂/n₂
[∵ Product of roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 is αβ = c/a]

recall.must_convey: That the product of the roots is c/a = −3/5, giving m₁m₂/3 = n₁n₂/(−5).
accept: the product of the roots is c over a which is minus three over five
m one m two over n one n two is minus three fifths
rearrange it as m one m two over three equals n one n two over minus five
product of roots c by a
this relates m one m two and n one n two

steps.why: Writing the result as a chain of equal fractions is what lets the second quadratic's result be joined onto it in the final step.
common_mistakes: Using −b/a, the SUM of the roots, instead of c/a.
Losing the minus sign on the 5.

steps.label: Eliminate n to get a quadratic in l/m
steps.margin_note: Three marks. The same move with a different letter removed, giving a second quadratic whose roots are l₁/m₁ and l₂/m₂.
steps.memory_tip: The same move with a different letter removed, giving roots l₁/m₁ and l₂/m₂.
lines: Substituting this value of n in (2), we get  −2m(l + m) − 3l(l + m) − 5lm = 0
This is a quadratic equation in l/m; its roots are taken as  l₁/m₁,  l₂/m₂

recall.must_convey: That eliminating n gives 3l² + 10lm + 2m² = 0, whose roots' product gives l₁l₂/2 = m₁m₂/3.
accept: eliminate n this time and divide by m squared
the product of the roots is two over three
l one l two over two equals m one m two over three
n ni eliminate chesi malli same cheyyali
this gives the second relation

steps.why: Each elimination produces one of the three products. Two eliminations are enough because the chain of equal fractions then links all three.
common_mistakes: Eliminating l again and getting the same information twice.
Reading the product of roots as b/a.

steps.label: Combine and test l₁l₂+m₁m₂+n₁n₂
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Chain (3) and (4) into one string of equal fractions, call the common value k, and add. Two lines are perpendicular exactly when that sum is zero.
steps.memory_tip: Chain the results into one string of equal fractions, call it k, and add. Zero means perpendicular.
lines: From (3) and (4), we get  l₁l₂/2 = m₁m₂/3 = n₁n₂/(−5) = k  (say)

lines.text: Hence proved that the two lines are perpendicular

recall.must_convey: That l₁l₂ + m₁m₂ + n₁n₂ = 2k + 3k − 5k = 0, so the lines are perpendicular.
accept: set the three equal fractions to k and add them
two k plus three k minus five k is zero
the sum of the products is zero so the lines are perpendicular
moodintini k ga pettesi add chesthe zero vasthundi
hence perpendicular

steps.why: The three coefficients of the original second relation, 2, 3 and −5, ARE the three products up to the common factor k — and they were chosen to add to zero, which is the whole question.
common_mistakes: Adding the coefficients of the wrong relation.
Concluding perpendicular without showing the sum is zero.
